claims: Most Kickstarter campaigns fail because they burn money before learning nobody wants the product (Google AI overview: ~40-43% of campaigns fail)
Creator did a version of this and 'it kind of worked', but actual Zoom conversations with customers were way more helpful
how_to_steps: Get a contact data source (Apollo / Prospeo)
Prompt Claude: 'Find three work audiences for this [product]. Show me a few sample fits' -> e.g. Developers, Designers, Consultants
Sign up ~10 sending mailboxes on Google Workspace and connect them to an email sequencer
Have Claude write marketing emails per audience showing different product concepts (e.g. Portrait coding screen, Dual-screen extender, Portable pen display, Client presentation screen)
Have Claude 'Build the tracking page before we send anything' (landing page + event collector; events offer_clicked, page_loaded, show_me_pressed)
Send as a forwarded-looking email ('Fwd: A second screen, anywhere' with Solo setup / Team setup links)
Ask Claude to 'Filter the robot clicks before you compare the audiences' (scanner/rapid-click/separate-events rules)
Ask 'Which audience and version worked best after filtering?' -> pick strongest candidate, retest head-to-head on fresh contacts
Still talk to real customers on Zoom
on_screen_only: Google search 'why do most kickstarter campaigns fail' with AI Overview and Reddit r/kickstarter result 'Most Kickstarter projects don't fail because of marketing. They fail long...'

Gmail: 'Fwd: A second screen, anywhere' from 'me to Josh': 'hey Josh, found you on LinkedIn and t... might be relevant to you. Begin forwarded message: From: Product team <hello@example...>' with buttons 'Solo setup' / 'Team setup'

Claude: 'Which audience and version worked best after filtering?' -> 'Strongest candidate: de... version B... intervals overlap... Next: retest B against A on fresh developers'

cta: follow; 'open sourcing all of my AI ideas for free'

relevance.why: A concrete, cheap demand-validation loop runnable from Claude Desktop with MCP-connected data sources; relevant before building any new app. The fake 'Fwd:' email is deceptive cold outreach (CAN-SPAM/deliverability risk) and the creator himself admits Zoom calls beat it

implement_score.why: Doable in a weekend (Apollo MCP + landing page + PostHog events + Claude analysis), but the forwarded-email trick is spammy and could burn domain reputation; better to adapt the structure (3 audiences x N concept variants, bot-filtered click analysis) with honest outreach

gap.what: New: a pre-build demand test using Claude + Apollo/Prospeo + email sequencer + click-event analysis with bot filtering. Liked set had website-listening funnels and hook testing but not pre-launch audience/concept validation

verify: Apollo/Prospeo pricing and whether their MCP/API free tiers cover contact export
Deceptive 'Fwd:' cold emails: CAN-SPAM, GDPR and Google Workspace sending limits / domain-reputation risk
Sample sizes needed for click-rate differences to be meaningful (video shows 'intervals overlap, no winner yet')
